faq.a: Mukhtar is associated with the Arabic form مختار, whose core sense is mukhtar; chosen, elected.

faq.q: What is the origin of Mukhtar?
faq.a: Mukhtar is associated with Arabic. Mukhtar is Arabic مُخْتَار (Mukhtār) 'chosen, elected', from the root خ ي ر (kh-y-r). The source gloss 'Chosen One' is consistent. Same name as mukhtaar.
Yes — the underlying form مختار is Arabic.
Mukhtar can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.q: What does Mukhtar mean in Persian?

faq.q: What are the variants of Mukhtar?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Mukhtar, mukhtar. Script forms are مختار, मुख़्तार.

faq.q: Is Mukhtar a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
